title: evidence_validation_result.json -- internal cross-document consistency log v0.1
description: Produced by consistency-check. Historical record of what was checked, not something downstream stages read past on their own -- the conflict-ledger gate (_conflict_ledger.json, check_conflicts_clear) is what actually controls progression, see harness-guardrails P6. PoC dev-phase decision: logs every field checked, consistent or not, not just findings -- narrow to findings-only once the harness is past PoC (see known-gaps.md).

topic.description: What was compared. e.g. "accident_date across DOC_001/DOC_002"

conflict_candidate_id.description: The claim-analysis conflict candidate this check judged, e.g. "CAC_0001". Lets a downstream reader match a check back to the claim_facts field that raised it without parsing `topic`. Null when the check did not come from a candidate.

field_id.description: The claim_facts field the candidate belongs to, e.g. "primary_diagnosis". Null when the check is not field-scoped.

values_compared.description: Each source's stated value for this topic, with attribution.

result.description: How the comparison came out. `consistent` means the two readings state the same fact -- the candidate was WITHDRAWN and a consumer may elect one reading. `contested_not_decisive` means the readings genuinely differ but the difference changes no decision (`not_material`): the disagreement is real and must NOT be promoted to a settled value. `inconsistent` means confirmed, and carries a conflict_id. Until 2026-08-21 `not_material` was written as `consistent`, so a real dispute was indistinguishable from a wording variance and stage 7 elected one side of it as fact -- on CASE_704 section 4 printed DOC_006's 'victim walked normally' as established while DOC_008 p4 said the opposite.

conflict_id.description: The _conflict_ledger.json entry this check raised. Required (non-null) when result is inconsistent; must be null when consistent.
